evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Groupoid (C : Category) : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := @Isomorphism C; homset := @iso_setoid C; id := @iso_id C; compose := @iso_compose C |}.

statement_record.book: A groupoid is a category in which every arrow is an isomorphism; equivalently a generalized group whose multiplication is defined only when domains and codomains match, groups being exactly the one-object groupoids.
statement_record.intree: Groupoid C is the category whose objects are those of C and whose morphisms x ~> y are the isomorphisms x ≅ y of C, with iso_id, iso_compose and the iso_setoid equivalence — i.e. the CORE of C, the canonical example of a groupoid.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the library provides a construction that yields a groupoid, but never defines groupoid-hood as a property, so no statement can be quantified over groupoids, and it is not even proved that every morphism of Groupoid C is invertible.

gap: There is no predicate or class expressing "every morphism of this category is an isomorphism" — nothing can be said of an arbitrary groupoid. The name Groupoid is bound instead to one particular construction (the core of a given C). Also missing: any lemma that every arrow of Groupoid C is invertible (iso_sym is available in Theory/Isomorphism.v but is never applied to state this); the identification of groups with one-object groupoids; and any category Grpd of groupoids (Construction/Groupoid.v's own header concedes "no standalone category of groupoids exists in-tree, so the adjunction remark in the header above remains prose rather than a theorem").

evidence.intree_statement: Class EquivalenceOfCategories {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) := { quasi_inverse : D ⟶ C; equivalence_counit : F ◯ quasi_inverse ≈ Id[D]; equivalence_unit : Id[C] ≈ quasi_inverse ◯ F }.
Definition Nat_Isos_to_Equivalence {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) (G : D ⟶ C) (counit_iso : F ◯ G ≅[Fun] Id[D]) (unit_iso : Id[C] ≅[Fun] G ◯ F) : EquivalenceOfCategories F.

Definition Equivalence_to_Cat_Iso {C D : Category} {F : C ⟶ D} (E : EquivalenceOfCategories F) : C ≅[Cat] D := @Build_Isomorphism Cat C D F quasi_inverse equivalence_counit (symmetry equivalence_unit).

statement_record.book: An equivalence of categories is a pair of functors E : C ⟶ D, F : D ⟶ C together with natural isomorphisms α : 1_C ≅ F∘E and β : 1_D ≅ E∘F; F is a pseudo-inverse of E and C ≃ D. It generalizes isomorphism of categories by replacing the strict identities 1_C = GF, 1_D = FG with natural isomorphisms.

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem FF_ESO_Equivalence `(F : C ⟶ D) `{@Full C D F} `{@Faithful C D F} `{@EssentiallySurjective C D F} : EquivalenceOfCategories F. Proof. exact (@Build_EquivalenceOfCategories C D F (ff_eso_inverse F) (ff_eso_counit F) (ff_eso_unit F)). Defined.
Theorem Equivalence_Full `(E : @EquivalenceOfCategories C D F) : Full F.
Theorem Equivalence_Faithful `(E : @EquivalenceOfCategories C D F) : Faithful F.

Theorem Equivalence_EssSurj `(E : @EquivalenceOfCategories C D F) : EssentiallySurjective F. Proof. exact (@Build_EssentiallySurjective C D F (fun d => quasi_inverse d) (fun d => equivalence_counit_at d)). Defined.
